turns.t: Hello. I've been very tired since the doctor put me on a new heart tablet, and I get out of breath. My daughter thinks I should say something.
I'm her daughter. She's been much slower since the tablet. She naps all afternoon now.
Thank you. Which tablet is it, Mrs Silva? ~
A beta-blocker, I think. It's called bisoprolol.
Do you remember how long ago it was started? ~
Two months ago, after the heart attack.
I'm sorry to hear that. When does the breathlessness happen?
Climbing stairs, and when I walk to the shops. I used to manage it fine.
Any chest pain, palpitations, or fainting?
No chest pain. No fainting.
Any wheeze, or swelling in the ankles?
No swelling. She does cough a little at night.
Does anyone smoke at home, or have you smoked?
I stopped when I had the heart attack.
Good for you. Do you have any allergies to medicines?
No, none.
Let me listen to your heart and lungs and feel your pulse. ~
Go on.
Your heart rate is slow, around fifty, and regular. Your lungs are clear, and your ankles are not swollen.
Is that too slow? ~
A bit slow, which can make people feel tired. It may be the beta-blocker, and her heart condition may also play a part.
Do I have to stop it? ~
Please don't stop it on your own, because it protects your heart after a heart attack. I'd like to check things first. ~
What checks? ~
I'll arrange a heart tracing today, and a blood test for anaemia and thyroid.
And then? ~
Depending on the results, I might lower the dose, or discuss it with her cardiologist.
All right. I'd rather feel less tired. ~
I'll phone you with the results. If you become faint, get chest pain, or are very breathless, call an ambulance.
We will. Thank you, doctor. ~
